notes: Fiscal year convention: Oracle fiscal years end on May 31; historical years are FY2023 (ended May 31, 2023), FY2024, and FY2025 (ended May 31, 2025). Forecast years are FY2026–FY2030.

EBIT in this package is proxied by GAAP Operating Income from the consolidated statements of operations (not EBIT as defined in every accounting schema). ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))

D&A in this package equals GAAP cash-flow addbacks: Depreciation + Amortization of intangible assets (not including amortization separately disclosed in operating expenses). ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))

NWC definition (for historical and forecast pct): constructed as (Trade receivables + Prepaid expenses & other current assets) − (Accounts payable + Accrued compensation & related benefits + Deferred revenues + Other current liabilities), excluding (i) Cash & cash equivalents and Marketable securities from current assets and (ii) current notes payable & other borrowings from current liabilities. This yields negative NWC consistent with deferred-revenue dynamics. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))
Tax rate, WACC, and terminal assumptions (except where explicitly guided for revenue/capex) are modeling choices and not guaranteed to match Oracle’s internal long-run assumptions.

FY2026 capex % of sales is directly implied from management’s FY2026 capex guidance ($50B) versus FY2026 revenue guidance ($67B). For FY2027–FY2030, capex % of sales tapers as a sober normalization assumption (no further capex guidance captured in retrieved materials). ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

NOL balance is set to federal net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $270 million disclosed in the tax footnote; NOL utilization percent is set to null because the retrieved filing excerpt does not explicitly state the 0.80 rule used in many models. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))
Current price is taken from the finance lookup available at/near 2026-03-21 research time (latest trade shown for 2026-03-20 close).

catalysts: Further upside (or downside) to FY2026/FY2027 revenue guidance driven by AI cloud demand and conversion of large-scale contracts. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Evidence that high guided capex translates into sustainable operating margin expansion as AI infrastructure ramps efficiently. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Sustained RPO momentum and improved operating leverage could reset market expectations for forward profitability. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))
company_overview: Oracle delivers enterprise applications and mission-critical databases, alongside cloud infrastructure and cloud applications (integrated suite approach).
Oracle’s FY2026 setup highlights a mix shift toward cloud growth while maintaining GAAP profitability through operating expense discipline.
Oracle reports in a unified consolidated structure with results driven by cloud services & license support, hardware, and services.
current_context: In Q3 FY26 (ended Feb. 28, 2026), Oracle reported total revenue of $17.2 billion (+22% in USD) and cloud revenue of $8.9 billion (+44% in USD). ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Management guided FY2026 revenue to $67 billion and FY2026 capital expenditures to $50 billion; it also raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $90 billion. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Q3 RPO ended at $553 billion (+325% YoY), supported by large-scale AI-related contract dynamics described by management. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth is anchored on management’s FY2026 and FY2027 revenue guidance, then tapers to more mature growth rates after 2027. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))
EBIT margin is modeled to improve gradually from FY2025 operating margin levels, consistent with scale benefits while sustaining significant AI/cloud investment.

D&A is held near recent sales-based levels; amortization of acquired intangibles remains a key driver of non-cash expense per GAAP cash flow reconciliation. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))

Working-capital dynamics are modeled as negative (deferred revenue-heavy model), based on historical balance-sheet construction excluding cash/investments and current debt. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))
Terminal value uses a Gordon growth approach with conservative long-run growth (2.5%), consistent with a mature enterprise software/cloud profile.
key_risks: Capex intensity risk: if AI infrastructure spend does not produce expected revenue/earnings, free cash flow and equity value could be pressured. ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Margin risk from competition or pricing pressure in cloud and applications; sustained investment could keep EBIT margin below model targets. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))
Tax and regulatory volatility risk, including changing effective tax rate vs. the modeled long-run assumption.

valuation_summary: DCF inputs use GAAP operating income as EBIT and GAAP cash-flow-derived D&A and capex, improving internal consistency with the source filings. ([s23.q4cdn.com](https://s23.q4cdn.com/440135859/files/doc_downloads/proxy-voting-material/2025/09/Oracle-2025-10-K-PDF-Final-9-26-25.pdf))

FY2026 capex intensity is explicitly reflected via management’s $50 billion capex guidance, with subsequent-year capex % of sales tapering to reflect normalization (assumption; no public guidance provided beyond FY2026). ([investor.oracle.com](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx))

Comps provide a directional check: peer forward P/E ratios cluster broadly in the mid-teens to low-20s and EV/EBITDA spans a wide SaaS/software range; valuation outputs should be interpreted alongside growth and capex intensity.
